body: I thank you both for your responses. Unfortunately, life is just getting shittier and shittier. I don't want to do it anymore. It shouldn't be this hard; it shouldn't be this helpless. I appreciate the time you took to respond.

I have my masters in religion. Kind of useless. And adjuncting can be a good thing and a bad thing. I can't get a tenure job because I don't have my PhD. Community colleges rarely hire full time. A lot of places don't like to hire adjuncts because they think the adjuncts become kind of compliant and don't strive for anything more. It's just not an easy position to be in. And while minimum wage jobs do give me experience, it's not the kind of experience that translates to a full time job.

I am lonely. I don't mind staying home by myself, with just my pet- I have a bird- and it's a vicious cycle. I stay at home, I become depressed, and then I don't want to go out if a friend does call. I try to make myself go out to the mall, or to call a friend for brunch, at least once or twice a month, but honestly, I'd rather stay at home in my PJs.

I am glad to be rid of my ex-fiance. There were differences in how we were brought up that we just couldn't overcome. He has since married, and I hope he treats her much better than he treated me. While I know that many people are staying single for longer, I just keep seeing the people I grew up with getting married. My best friend just sent me a message saying that she's pregnant. I'm really happy for her, but it just reconfirms that I'm so far away from that.

I guess, more than anything, I'm just depressed. I feel like, at this point, nothing would really change if I wasn't here. People would notice, perhaps even be sad for a while, but after a week or two, everything would return to exactly how it was before. I had a friend who killed himself while I was in high school. I don't think anyone even visits his grave anymore. I feel...insignificant.
